title: Using the Expectancy-Value-Cost Framework for Making More Engaging and Motivating Decisions on Tech-Based Innovation Education Teams
content:
This paper introduces a model and tool designed to aid undergraduate students in making 
better team-based decisions by considering their motivation and engagement. Collaborative tech- 
based projects require numerous decisions impacting team dynamics, including expectations, values, 
and costs, potentially causing demotivation and disengagement. Supported by theories like Self- 
Determination Theory and the Conflict-Theory Model of Decision-Making, this study identifies 
decision-related factors contributing to negative outcomes such as delays, dissatisfaction, low grades, 
and dropouts. The proposed MO-DM (Motivation-Oriented Decision-Making) model assesses how 
project decisions affect student motivation and engagement. For example, choosing a programming 
language by evaluating its impact on team motivation. This model anticipates demotivation, allowing 
monitoring by teachers and peers. Based on a systematic literature review and research involving 
209 students, tools like EVC, AMS, SCEQ, and AI for analyzing student interactions were used. 
Results showed a 12.51% increase in overall student motivation and engagement, with a 16.67% rise 
in intrinsic motivation (SDI). Student feedback was 82.86% positive, with 85.71% agreement (Fleiss’ 
Kappa). Pearson correlation coefficients exceeded 0.92, indicating strong consistency. The model 
is effective in enhancing motivation and engagement in collaborative decision-making contexts, 
applicable in academic and professional environments. An open-source, public tool was created to 
implement the model, with a presentation available here.
